description:
Advances: ancora.derive, ancora.gate

Findings: F1 (Critical, distributed C1), F4 (High, security H1), F24 rides along (Medium, data M2). Consensus CF1 in ~/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-04/ancora-xla-post-ship-hardening/20260904-061300-consolidated.md.

Deliverable:
Two reproduced defects with one root cause: a git-supplied name is carried as an opaque string from the subprocess into a map key and a blob spec with no point where it becomes a validated relative path.
(a) `git diff --name-status` and `git status --porcelain` run without `-z` at lib/ancora/derive/change_set.ex:56-66 and :101-114, so any path git C-quotes (non-ASCII byte, space, tab, quote, backslash) is stored as the quoted literal. Against a repo containing lib/café.ex the change set holds "lib/caf\303\251.ex"; ModuleLocator.base_sources falls through to :unchanged so base == head and no drift can ever be detected; Compare.changed_definition? filters the binding out; `mix spec.check` prints result=pass. Silent fail-open.
(b) lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex:164-180 parses git cat-file --batch's "<request> missing" reply by splitting on spaces, so a request spec containing a space is read as a malformed frame. One untracked file named "my notes.txt" flips `mix spec.check` from result=pass to an unhandled RuntimeError ("gate assembly failed: {:cat_file_batch_bad_header, ...}" raised at gate.ex:466) with no verdict line. Reproduced end to end at e18fa05. Loud fail-closed with no contract.
Fix: add `-z` to both git invocations and parse NUL-delimited records (which never quote); resolve change-set paths to object ids through the existing Git.ls_tree_entries/3 and fetch by OID in prefetch/2 (change_set.ex:81), matching what BaseView already does on this branch; tag Git.read_blob/2's second argument as {:path, p} or {:oid, o} and delete the 40/64-hex regex heuristic and read_spec/2 (git.ex:14, :90-92; this is F24 and it is required because the OID fetch makes the ambiguity live); parse the missing reply from its right-hand end; add a {:cat_file_batch_bad_header, _} clause to gate_error/1 so any residual bad frame reaches the operator as tier=env with a verdict line, never a stack trace. Backstop: refuse any path that still arrives wrapped in double quotes rather than storing it.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/derive/change_set_test.exs, test/ancora/git_batch_port_test.exs, test/ancora/git_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate, each through a real git fixture and the real gate or CLI:
  1. An untracked file whose name contains a space: `mix spec.check` ends `spec.check result=pass` with exit 0 (today: RuntimeError, no verdict). Mutation the test must kill: restore the space-split parse.
  2. A changed lib/café.ex whose definition changed between base and head: the derived transition/drift finding fires (today: nothing). Mutation: drop `-z` from either git call; the test must fail.
  3. A committed file whose path contains a space, changed between base and head: prefetch resolves it by OID and the comparison sees the real base bytes. Mutation: fetch by path spec again; the test must fail.
  4. A malformed batch frame that still reaches the gate ends tier=env with a verdict line. Mutation: remove the gate_error clause; the test must fail.
  5. Git.read_blob/2 with {:path, <40 hex chars>} reads the path, not an object. Mutation: restore the regex; the test must fail.
- Spec edit required in-diff (substantive, not an acknowledgment): ancora.derive (change_set_union or base_reads_batched) shall state that change-set paths are read NUL-delimited, never stored quoted, and resolved to object ids before any blob read; ancora.gate (preflight_hard_fails or the env-tier statement) shall state that a malformed cat-file frame is an environment failure with a verdict line. Decision-record edit: an affects entry or Consequences note on ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state or a new ADR; name what changed.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: compile-graph-scoped checks only (`mix test --stale` or the named files) plus `mix spec.validate`; run `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` as a dev-loop check as soon as the spec edit exists, before either capped final-tier run.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, the named test files, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix deps.unlock --check-unused`, `mix spec.check --base e18fa05`, run-until-green. Full suite runs at the orchestrator's merge gate.
  - Verifier tier: `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` plus targeted selections; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test that fails under the named mutation; prove each ordered test both ways and report the numbers
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh: the substantive requirement or scenario edit named below lands in the same diff with its decision-record edit; never a Spec-Ack trailer; never weaken a must
  - Fixtures never call production functions (use test/support or System.cmd); under file-scoped derivation a stray call binds a subject
  - Grader scratch discipline applies to you too: work only in this worktree, address it by absolute path
- Call-site Integration: the production callers are ChangeSet.compute/1 and ChangeSet.prefetch/2 reached from Gate.check/2 and Review; the proving tests are the gate/CLI fixtures above, not unit tests of the parser alone.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/base_view.ex (F3, ancora-kzw, and F9/F36 on ancora-d16)
- lib/ancora/review/**, lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, lib/ancora/trailer.ex, lib/ancora/config.ex, lib/mix/tasks/**
Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/derive/change_set.ex, lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex, lib/ancora/git.ex, lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex (only if the OID path forces a signature change)
- lib/ancora/gate.ex (gate_error/1 clause and the prefetch call site only)
- test/ancora/**, test/mix/tasks/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (substantive edits named above; never weakening a must)
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (binding-aware clause: derivation is file-scoped, so acknowledgment edits only, one substantive sentence describing what this ticket changed as that subject observes it, verified by execution; if the subject observes nothing, say so in the completion record and stop)
- .spec/decisions/** (every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; write a real contract statement, never a hollow line)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No constraint of entry paths to the materialization root (that is ancora-kzw; do not half-fix it here). No change to BaseView's read path. No new dependency. No change to the batch-port accumulation loop (F9, deferred). Do not rebase; base stays e18fa05.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes (`mix spec.check --base e18fa05` result=pass)
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

IMPLEMENTED
Session: 41r1-i1-adec463e
Log: /Users/mz/.local/state/agentic-runs/ancora/ancora-41r.1/codex-41r1-i1-adec463e/log

Commit: d00f2f882df4afd0cecc4b206732d3c88c7e2cfd
Files touched: .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state.md, .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, lib/ancora/derive/change_set.ex, lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/git.ex, lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex, test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/ancora/git_batch_port_test.exs, test/ancora/git_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
Tests added: Ancora.Git.BatchPortTest "fetch parses a missing path containing spaces from the right"; Ancora.GitTest "read_blob treats a tagged 40-hex path as a path"; Ancora.GateTest "gate detects drift in a UTF-8 library path"; Ancora.GateTest "change-set prefetch resolves a spaced path to its base OID"; Mix.Tasks.Spec.CheckTest "an untracked path containing a space keeps spec.check green"; Mix.Tasks.Spec.CheckTest "a malformed cat-file frame emits an environment verdict"
Spec acknowledgment: substantive edits to ancora.derive and ancora.gate, with a Consequences update to ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state; no Spec-Ack trailer
Verification tier: change-scoped: mix compile --warnings-as-errors; test/ancora/derive/change_set_test.exs, test/ancora/git_batch_port_test.exs, test/ancora/git_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs; mix format --check-formatted; mix deps.unlock --check-unused; mix spec.check --base e18fa05. Full-system proof deferred to the merge gate and PR CI.
Final-tier runs: 1

Summary: Change-set paths now use NUL-delimited Git output, reject quoted fallback data, resolve base paths to OIDs before batch reads, and keep path and OID references explicit. Malformed batch frames now reach the CLI as tier=env with a final verdict. Mutation proofs, each run alone: spaced missing-frame parser 1 failure mutated and 1 pass restored, UTF-8 path 2 failures for removing each -z flag and 1 pass restored, spaced-path OID prefetch 1 failure mutated and 1 pass restored, malformed-frame gate clause 1 failure mutated and 1 pass restored, 40-hex tagged path 1 failure mutated and 1 pass restored; the real CLI spaced-untracked fixture also passed 1 selected test. All current lesson lines were checked against the diff. Other impacted subjects reported only existing unresolved-call info and observed no drift, growth, or shrink from this change.

TEST_CRITIC: FAIL

Blocking: test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:34 (global PATH mutation in an async module) and test/ancora/gate_test.exs:444,484 (drift asserted by code membership only, never by the file the ticket ordered).

RAN (stage worktree /Users/mz/src/ancora-41r.1, HEAD d00f2f8): git_batch_port_test.exs + git_test.exs -> 17 tests, 0 failures. gate_test.exs:420 and :448 -> 2 tests, 0 failures. spec_check_test.exs:22 and :34 -> 2 tests, 0 failures. All six new assertions are reachable and execute.

=== BLOCKING ===

B1 [critical, isolation] spec_check_test.exs:34 "a malformed cat-file frame emits an environment verdict"
The test does System.put_env("PATH", wrapper_dir <> ":" <> original_path) and restores it in on_exit. The module is `use Ancora.TestCase` with no async option, so it is async: true (ancora_case.exs defaults async to true). PATH is VM-global: for the ~2 s the subprocess runs, every concurrently running async module resolves `git` to the fake shim, both for run_mix_subprocess children and for in-VM Ancora.Git.run (git.ex:28 calls System.find_executable("git") at call time). RunContext opens a cat-file --batch port by default (run_context.ex:47), so a concurrent module that reaches the gate gets "malformed frame" and fails for an unrelated reason. Async modules that touch git during a run: spec_status_test, spec_next_test, spec_review_test, spec_validate_test, index_test, append_only_test, review_test, fresh_adopter_test.
I could NOT reproduce a cross-module failure: I ran spec_check + spec_status + spec_next + spec_review + index together twice (40 tests, 0 failures both times, seeds 334190 and 348724). So this is a latent race, not an observed flake. It is still a defect by construction and the fix is one word.
Fix: `use Ancora.TestCase, async: false` on the module. That is already the house precedent - git_test.exs pulls the same PATH trick ("run returns data when git is absent from PATH") and is async: false. Alternative: teach run_mix_subprocess an :env option and pass PATH per-call instead of mutating the VM.

B2 [warning, precision] gate_test.exs:444 and gate_test.exs:484
Both new gate tests assert only `assert "derived/drift" in findings_codes(report.all_findings)`. findings_codes/1 (ancora_case.exs:74) maps findings to codes, so this proves "some drift fired somewhere", not "drift fired for lib/café.ex". Ancora.Finding carries :subject and :file (finding.ex:11), and compare.ex:153 populates both on every derived/drift. The house pattern in this same file at gate_test.exs:655 already asserts across fields with Enum.any?.
This matters here specifically: the bug class is a path stored under the wrong name. A finding attributed to the C-quoted literal "lib/caf\303\251.ex" would satisfy the current assertion. The mutation is still killed (each fixture has exactly one lib source, so no drift can fire at all when -z is dropped), but the assertion does not name what it proves.
Fix, gate_test.exs:444:
  assert Enum.any?(report.all_findings, fn f ->
           f.code == "derived/drift" and f.file == "lib/café.ex" and f.subject == "sample.subject"
         end)
and the same at :484 with "lib/my sample.ex".

=== UNVERIFIED BY READING (needs a mutation run) ===

U1 spec_check_test.exs:22 "an untracked path containing a space keeps spec.check green"
The ticket names the mutation "restore the space-split parse". Reading says this test no longer depends on that parse. New prefetch (change_set.ex:81-99) resolves entries through Git.ls_tree_entries against base; an untracked path is not in the base tree, so Map.fetch(oids, path) returns :error, the entry is recorded :missing, and no read_blob and no port request is ever issued for "my notes.txt". The test does reproduce the reported bug at e18fa05 (where prefetch fetched every entry by path spec), so it is an honest regression test - but post-fix it no longer exercises a space-sensitive code path.
Mutation for the verifier: revert missing_id/1 in lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex to `case String.split(header, " ")` with the `[id, "missing"]` clause, then run `mix test test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:22`. My prediction from reading: STAYS GREEN. If so, behavior 1's named mutation is killed only by git_batch_port_test.exs:110, not by the CLI fixture. That is acceptable coverage, but the ticket's test-to-mutation mapping should be corrected in the completion record.

U2 gate_test.exs:448, the OID assertion
`assert {:oid, oid} in collect_git_reads([])` depends on erlang trace delivery from the test process. It executed and passed in my run, and it fails loud (empty list) rather than silently if the read moves to another process, so there is no false-pass risk. Reading says the named mutation kills it.
Mutation for the verifier: change change_set.ex:92 to `Git.read_blob(ctx, {:path, path})`, run `mix test test/ancora/gate_test.exs:448`. Expected: FAIL on the {:oid, _} membership.

=== VERDICTS ON THE POINTS RAISED ===

Fixture honesty - PASS. I reproduced the writes outside the repo and dumped the bytes: "café.ex" lands as 63 61 66 c3 a9 2e 65 78 (real UTF-8 é, not an escape) and "my sample.ex" as 6d 79 20 73 ... (real 0x20). write_files/1 (ancora_case.exs:47) is plain File.write!, and commit_all/git! (ancora_case.exs:84,89) shell out via System.cmd with an argv list, no shell and no quoting helper. The batch-port test's spaced name goes through TmpGitRepo.write!/commit! the same way. The 40-hex test creates a real 40-character filename and commits it.

Base bytes on the prefetch test - PARTIAL PASS. The test pins the exact OID from `git rev-parse <base>:lib/my sample.ex` and asserts read_blob was called with {:oid, that_oid}. A blob OID is the identity of its bytes, and derived/drift only fires if the comparison actually saw :before against :after, so the base bytes are established transitively. The test never asserts the byte string itself. I am satisfied; if you want it explicit, add `assert {:ok, "defmodule Sample do\n  def value, do: :before\nend\n"} = Git.read_blob(ctx, {:oid, oid})` before the gate run.

Malformed-frame fixture honesty - PASS. The shim intercepts only `git -C <root> cat-file --batch` (positional $3/$4, which matches BatchPort.open's exact args at batch_port.ex:36) and exec's the real git for everything else, with real_git captured before PATH is touched. No production code is mutated to produce the bad frame. The test asserts status 1, the operator message, the exact verdict line "spec.check result=fail tier=env errors=0 warnings=0", and no RuntimeError on stderr. Positional coupling to argv order is fail-loud, not false-pass: if the args change, the shim falls through to real git and the message assertion fails.

Untracked-space test asserting both - PASS. status == 0 and List.last(lines(stdout)) == "spec.check result=pass" by equality, plus refute stderr =~ "RuntimeError".

Fixtures parsing git status/diff - PASS, none. Fixtures call git for init/add/commit/rev-parse only and trim rev-parse output. Note (pre-existing, unchanged by this diff): test/support/tmp_git_repo.exs drives fixture setup through the production Ancora.Git.run/2, so the new batch-port and git tests build their repos with the module family under test. Out of this ticket's scope; flagging only.

Source-text pinning - acceptable. The only pinned production string is "git cat-file batch returned a malformed frame" from gate.ex:484. That is the operator-facing CLI contract and matches the house style elsewhere in these files. The load-bearing guard is the verdict-line equality, which is behavior.

Weakening of existing tests - NONE. `git diff e18fa05..HEAD --numstat -- test/` shows zero deletions except 4 lines in git_test.exs, all mechanical retags of read_blob's second argument to {:path, _} / {:oid, _} forced by the signature change. The 4 MB payload fixture at git_batch_port_test.exs:129 is untouched.

=== NOTE FOR THE API REVIEWER (not a test failure) ===
After this diff no production caller passes {:path, _} to Git.read_blob. change_set.ex:92 passes {:oid, _}; base_view.ex:84 passes a bare binary and lands on the untagged fallback clause `blob_reference(_base, oid) when is_binary(oid)`. So the tagged path branch has no production call site, and the fallback clause that preserves the old ambiguity has no test. Behavior 5 is a unit behavior the ticket asked for explicitly, so the test satisfies the contract - but if the intent was to delete the ambiguity, base_view.ex:84 should pass {:oid, entry.oid} and the bare-binary clause should go.

title: Git-supplied path names crash the gate or hide files from the change set
